places.gf_detail: Ask. Biryani, rice and South Indian dosa are not wheat-based, but naan is, curry bases are not described, and staff speak mainly English (2024). No gluten-free claim from the restaurant.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists "vegetarian options", and there are lentil and spinach curries, dosa with potato masala and tomato rasam. Ghee, butter and cream are not ruled out.

places.cuisine: North and South Indian since 1999 · dosa with potato masala, tomato rasam · butter chicken, keema, lentil and spinach curries · chicken biryani (huge) · tandoori chicken · crispy naan · spice level 1–5 · Mithila set ¥1,650 · Kingfisher, mango lassi
places.notes: [Indian · a 1999 Indian restaurant above Dotonbori] A long-running, 45-seat Indian restaurant up a flight of stairs on Dotonbori, its sign hidden among the neon near the Glico man. The staff are Indian and English works better than Japanese. Beyond the usual curries (butter chicken, keema, lentil, spinach) and crisp naan, there is South Indian cooking: a dosa wrapped round potato masala and a tangy tomato rasam. The chicken biryani is big enough for two, and the kitchen will pack leftovers. The Mithila set (two curries, naan, salad) was ¥1,650 in August 2025, up from ¥880. Choose spice 1–5, since the standard level is very mild. Tabelog flags vegetarian options. Smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: An Indian-run restaurant; 2024 reviewers note the staff are Indian and mostly speak English.
chef_bio.specialty: Biryani; South Indian dosa and rasam.

anecdotes.text: "Dosa, a South Indian dish similar to a crepe, was served wrapped around potato masala… Rasam, a South Indian soup, had a base of tomato, offering a light broth." — December 2022.
"The chicken biryani was more refined than what I had in Little India, Malaysia, and it was served in a large size, enough for two people." — September 2026.

places.notes: [Jamaican · gluten-free Jamaican cooking in Kitahorie] A tiny, cheerful Jamaican kitchen in Kitahorie. Celiac reviewers say it is 100% gluten-free, with a dedicated fryer, and it is also dairy-free with lots of vegan dishes. The owner cooks everything in view and is careful about gluten, even flagging that the beer isn't safe. Order the jerk chicken plate with crisp potato wedges (smoky, slightly spicy, well cooked), a jerk chicken bean wrap, tapas, or the popular nachos, which sell out after lunch. places.notes: [Ramen · Minami's 1971 shio ramen and gyoza counter] An 11-seat counter in a back-alley building in Ura-Namba, serving ramen and gyoza since 1971 and still a classic end to a night of drinking. The ramen is a clear, gentle chicken-bone shio, made by pouring a yellow tare into the bowl, then the sparkling broth, with sesame, bean sprouts, green onion and thin straight noodles. The chashu ramen was ¥1,200 in September 2026, and the wonton noodles ¥1,100. The hand-made gyoza (8 for ¥400) are light and chewy, and media favourites. Wontons are made fresh and can sell out. One regular has visited more than 140 times. It was long run by a married couple; the owner now trains a younger team. Evenings only, closed Sundays, cash only.

chef_bio.background: Run by a husband-and-wife team before the pandemic, then by the owner with newly trained young staff (January 2025 and September 2026 reviews); no source names the owner.

places.cuisine: Bite-sized Osaka gyoza · original garlic gyoza ¥450–500 · juicy shrimp gyoza ¥550 (try with salt) · squid, potato-cheese and vegetable gyoza · salted tamago rice ¥990 · draft beer ¥600 · late nights · smoking allowed
places.notes: [Gyoza · bite-sized Osaka gyoza across from Amza] The main shop of Yasudaya, an 18-seat gyoza izakaya across from Amza in Sennichimae, open late and lively, with multilingual menus. The gyoza are small enough to eat in one bite, so order several kinds. The original garlic gyoza (¥450–500 in October 2026) has a crisp, thin skin and a strong garlic punch. The juicy shrimp gyoza (¥550) is best with salt, as staff suggest. There are also squid, potato-cheese and vegetable versions. One diner found the potato-cheese and vegetable ones not to their taste. Wash them down with ¥600 draft beer and finish with salted tamago rice (¥990). Tables are cramped and service can be distracted. Smoking allowed, closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.origin: Main shop (Tabelog); the first Sennichimae Yasudaya opened in June 2011 (Tabelog remarks)
chef_bio.background: Yasudaya gyoza (yasuda-ya.jp); Tabelog introduction: "A Man Devoted to Gyoza! Crafted by a Naniwa Artisan".

anecdotes.text: "Original Garlic Gyoza JPY 450… These gyoza feature a crispy thin skin filled with a strong punch of garlic… Juicy Shrimp Gyoza JPY 550… The staff recommended enjoying it with salt." — October 2026.
"We ordered 4 servings of regular pan-fried gyoza, 1 serving each of squid gyoza and shrimp gyoza… Osaka-style gyoza is perfect on its own!" — September 2026.

places.cuisine: Tonkotsu ramen ¥980 with three chashu and half an egg · special ramen ~¥1,000 · spicy Sichuan tonkotsu · miso · tsukemen · negi ramen ¥1,080 · ramen and kara-age set ¥1,400 · gyoza ¥450, fried rice ¥600 · free kimchi · 24 h
places.notes: [Ramen · a new 24-hour tonkotsu in Sōemonchō] Opened in December 2025 in the old Daikichi Ramen spot in Sōemonchō, with a bright sign that is welcome at 4:30 am. The tonkotsu ramen (¥980, April 2026) comes with three slices of chashu and half an egg over thin noodles, rich but not heavy. The special ramen adds wood ear and bean sprouts, and a spicy Sichuan version builds slowly. There's also a miso version that tastes like miso tonkotsu, and a glossy, medium-thin tsukemen whose dip one diner wanted richer. Free kimchi arrives as soon as you order, and stirring it into the bowl is the move. Sides are cheap and good: fluffy chashu fried rice (¥600), gyoza (¥450), kara-age sets. Buy a ticket at the machine.

places.cuisine: Kinryu's two-item menu: ramen ¥900 or chashu ramen · gentle, cloudy pork-bone broth · straight medium-thin noodles · unlimited free rice, kimchi, spicy garlic chives and chopped garlic · tatami-covered chairs · table seating
places.notes: [Ramen · Kinryu off Ebisubashi-suji, with free rice] The Ebisubashi branch of the dragon-sign chain, just off the shopping street. The menu is just ramen (¥900 in October 2026, ¥800 in 2025) or chashu ramen. Buy a ticket, swap it for a number tag, and help yourself at the self-service counter: unlimited white rice, kimchi, spicy garlic chives and chopped garlic. The broth is a gentle, cloudy pork bone that goes down easily after drinking, over straight medium-thin noodles with three thin slices of chashu. It becomes "your style" once loaded with garlic. The tatami-covered chairs are a Kinryu signature. Some find the rice soft. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Kinryu Ramen chain.
chef_bio.specialty: Light tonkotsu with free kimchi, chives, garlic and rice.

anecdotes.text: "It's a pork bone broth, but on the lighter side—'gentle pork bone'. Despite being cloudy, it's not heavy at all. It goes down smoothly even after drinking." — October 2026, chashu ramen.
"Ramen JPY 900… Unlimited free white rice! Unlimited free garlic chive kimchi! Unlimited free napa cabbage kimchi!" — October 2026.

places.name: こうてい麺 大ちゃん (Kotei Men Daichan)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; gyoza.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken-bone broth, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–6:00, until sold out; closed Sundays (Tabelog). Tabelog lists AMEX, but a September 2026 reviewer says cash only. Smoking allowed (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Light, clear chicken-bone shio ramen · butter and seasoned-egg toppings · slightly curly medium-thick noodles · mizuna and green onion · shoyu ramen · chashu don with an eel-sauce-like sweetness · cabbage-sweet gyoza · counter, open to 6 am
places.notes: [Ramen · a back-alley shio counter in Shinsaibashi, to 6 am] A long-running counter shop down an alley in Shinsaibashi's drinking district (one diner returned after 20 years), open from 6 pm until 6 am or sell-out. The order is the shio ramen: a light, clear chicken-bone broth with a gentle salt tare, slightly curly medium-thick noodles, mizuna and green onion. Melted butter or a seasoned egg rounds it out. The chashu don is sweet like eel sauce, a nice contrast, and the gyoza are sweet with cabbage. Opinions vary: some find it plain, and one reviewer thought the shoyu lacked character despite the media stickers. There is also a Daichan in Namba. Smoking allowed. Cash may be needed.

chef_bio.background: A reviewer notes "a Daichan in Namba and another in Shinsaibashi" (October 2025); no source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "The broth seems to be made from chicken bones, combined with a gentle salt tare, resulting in a light and clear soup. The noodles are slightly curly and medium-thick… Adding the melted butter enhances the richness." — April 2026, first visit in about 20 years.
"The 'Chashu Don' is richly flavored with a sweetness and depth reminiscent of eel sauce. The contrast with the light Sio Ramen is intriguing." — October 2025.

places.notes: [Ramen · a big Kamukura by NGK] A 67-seat Kamukura on a corner of the Namba shopping street near NGK, since 2024, run on touch panels and an automatic payment machine. The bowl is the chain's light, slightly sweet broth with plenty of napa cabbage, easy to eat yet, one diner said, deep and complex. Seasonal specials appear: a hot-and-sour ramen with cilantro (October 2026) and, in summer, a cold ramen that is better with yuzu. The fried rice and kara-age set is a guilty pleasure, and beer comes big. Points on the app earn free toppings. One summer visitor found the first-floor counter a little smelly.

chef_bio.background: Kamukura chain (kamukura.co.jp).

"At this location, you place your order using a touch panel inside and pay at an automatic payment machine… They have an app that allows you to earn points with each visit, and you can get free toppings." — October 2026.

places.name: ChocoLatta (ショコラッタ)
places.gf_detail: The shop calls itself a gluten-free gâteau-chocolat specialist (「グルテンフリーのガトーショコラ専門店」), made with naturally grown domestic rice flour and no wheat flour. FMGF marks it "Reported to be dedicated gluten-free", and celiac reviewers (October 2026) describe an entirely gluten-free menu: French toast, waffles, sandwiches, BLAT, bagels. Confirm, as the menu has grown beyond cakes.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the gâteau chocolat uses fermented butter (official site); bacon, sausage and egg dishes.
places.hours_raw: Official site: Mon–Sat 12:00–20:30, Sun 11:30–19:00, irregular closing days (announced on the blog). But FMGF reviewers in October 2026 describe early-opening breakfast, so the hours may have changed; check Instagram (@chocolatta2013).

places.cuisine: Gluten-free gâteau chocolat (rice flour, cane sugar, organic French and sustainable Belgian chocolate) · gluten-free breakfast: French toast, waffles, BLAT with egg, sandwiches, bagels · takeaway and online shop
places.notes: [Sweets · a gluten-free gâteau-chocolat café in Karahori] A small café in the retro Karahori district that began as a gluten-free gâteau-chocolat specialist. Its chocolate cake is made with naturally grown domestic rice flour, cane sugar, fermented butter and organic French and sustainable Belgian chocolate. It now also serves a gluten-free breakfast-and-lunch menu that celiac visitors rave about: French toast ("absolutely incredible"), waffles, a BLAT with egg, bacon and sausage plates, chicken sandwiches to take away. It is run by one person, so food can take a while, and it is pricey (about ¥5,000 for two plates and two coffees, October 2026). Only a few tables.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kansai-tuned iekei on Sennichimae-dōri] A 9-seat counter on Sennichimae-dōri, since 2011, serving a Yokohama iekei deliberately bent toward Osaka tastes. Some say the broth and noodle portions run small. Weekdays it opens only for dinner, but it runs until 5 am. Buy a ticket at the small machine outside.

The dry version, the original style, coats the noodles in a nutty sesame sauce with chili oil and numbing Sichuan pepper (¥1,100, 2025); adjust it with sansho and niboshi vinegar. One reviewer heard it is a popular tantanmen shop from the north of the city opening a southern branch.

places.notes: [Ramen · Nagoya-style mazesoba in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] Arashi's mazesoba shop reopened on 1 October 2026 about 200 m west of its old spot, now on two floors. Reviewers who knew it in Nagoya were glad to find it. The signature mazesoba (¥1,200 for 200 g, a 100 g small for ¥1,000) dresses thick, wavy, house-made whole-wheat noodles in a light salt sauce of chicken oil infused with dried shrimp and scallop. On top go an egg yolk, cubed roast chashu, mizuna, green onion, fish powder and nori, with a punch of garlic and chili. Taiwan mazesoba comes in curry and salt versions too. Mix from the bottom, then add kombu vinegar or shichimi. Ordering is by QR code. In the first weeks, staff were still finding their feet and payment was cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · a 50-seat Kamukura in Shinsaibashi] A long counter-only Kamukura on the Shinsaibashi side of Minami, open from 10 am to 6:30 am the next morning. It serves the chain's gentle, napa-cabbage-sweet broth that "felt like a warm hug" to one first-timer. The ajitama ramen was ¥980 in August 2026. Summer brings a cold version, slightly salty to stand up to the ice and served with yuzu juice to change the flavour, which regulars recommend on the hottest days. A dependable post-drinks stop, busy late at night.

chef_bio.background: Kamukura chain (kamukura.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The generous amount of napa cabbage was quite impressive. Taking a sip of the broth, I was greeted by the gentle sweetness of the cabbage." — August 2026, ajitama ramen ¥980.
"When chilled, the animal fats solidify, but it felt like they handled it well… It also comes with yuzu juice, which is perfect for changing up the flavor." — August 2026, cold ramen.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: whole-wheat noodles in a soy-sauce broth.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chashu (pork and chicken); bonito in the cold ramen.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30). Closed one Wednesday in most odd-numbered months (in 2026: 1 and 21 Jan, 18 Mar, 20 May, 15 Jul, 16 Sep, 18 Nov); short hours 31 Dec and 2 Jan (Tabelog). Pay at the entrance; cards accepted.
places.neighborhood: Namba Walk (underground) 1-bangai north street, Namba 2-chōme — 3 min west of Kintetsu Osaka-Namba
places.cuisine: Jinrui Mina Menrui's offshoot · shoyu ramen made from "just water and soy sauce" ¥990, clear yet intensely savoury · rare pork and chicken chashu · whole-wheat noodles · chilled "kin-kin" noodles with bonito broth and chili oil ¥970 · seared chashu rice ¥330 · free rice refills · 14 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Jinrui Mina Menrui's water-and-soy-sauce shoyu, under Namba] A 14-seat counter in the Namba Walk underground mall, the first shop of a newer brand from Osaka's famous queue magnet Jinrui Mina Menrui, since April 2023. The signature shoyu ramen (¥990, October 2026) is made, the shop says, from just water and soy sauce, with no stock. It pours clear, but reviewers find it punchy and deep with umami. Expect chewy whole-wheat noodles, beautifully rare pork and carefully cooked chicken chashu. Summer brings the ice-cold "kin-kin" noodles in a bonito broth drizzled with chili oil (¥970). Rice refills are free, and the special toppings add a free half serving of noodles. Pay at the entrance. One diner felt the bowl looked half-empty.

chef_bio.background: The next brand of the Osaka ramen shop Jinrui Mina Menrui (Tabelog introduction: "Minna Mina Menrui"); a direct branch, per an October 2026 review.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A simple yet rich soy sauce flavor made with just 'water and soy sauce,' without any broth" (Tabelog introduction).

anecdotes.text: "Perfect bowl with chewy whole wheat noodles, punchy bonito broth, and beautifully rare chashu!… unlimited rice refills for free, and with special and premium toppings, you can even get a half serving of extra noodles for free." — October 2026.

"I ordered the 'Chilled Kin-Kin Noodles' for JPY 970… the soup was ice-cold, paired with thin straight noodles, three slices of chicken breast, and drizzled with chili oil. I love the cold, bonito-flavored broth!" — September 2026.

places.name: 富喜製麺研究所 心斎橋店 (Fuki Seimen Kenkyusho Shinsaibashi)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: house-made whole-wheat noodles; soy-sauce dip.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: bonito-soy dipping sauce, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 21:00–6:00; closed Mondays (Tabelog). A July 2026 reviewer gives Sundays as the closing day instead, so check. Mobile ordering at the seat. Smoking allowed (Tabelog).

places.cuisine: Kumamoto noodle-maker's shop · kombu-water tsukemen with bonito-kombu dip ¥1,100 (large +¥150) · flat whole-wheat noodles · sudachi to finish · chuka soba · "Guilty Jirō" · rice dishes and sides · 9 pm–6 am
places.notes: [Tsukemen · a noodle-maker's kombu-water tsukemen, all night] A late-night branch of Fuki Seimen Kenkyusho, a noodle maker with roots in Kumamoto and shops in Tokyo and Osaka, open in Shinsaibashi since June 2025. After the Fukai branch closed in May 2026, it became the only Osaka shop. The draw is the noodles: flat, chewy whole-wheat noodles served soaking in kombu water, so taste a couple plain first. The bonito-kombu tsukemen (¥1,100, July 2026) comes with a sweetish, katsuo-forward soy dip that the kombu water doesn't dilute. Squeeze in sudachi as you go. There's also a chuka soba whose broth one diner finished, and a popular "Guilty Jirō". Order on your phone at the seat. Open 9 pm to 6 am; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Fuki Seimen Kenkyusho, a noodle maker with shops in Kumamoto, Tokyo and Osaka (official site title); a June 2026 reviewer calls it a direct branch of a long-established Kumamoto noodle shop and says the first Osaka shop (Fukai) closed on 24 May 2026.

anecdotes.text: "Katsuo Kombu Water Tsukemen JPY 1,100… They were flat, made with whole wheat, and had a nice chew—delicious! The dipping sauce was on the sweeter side, with a strong katsuo soy sauce flavor that didn't get diluted by the kombu water." — July 2026.
"You can really tell this is a shop directly operated by a noodle manufacturer." — June 2026.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: minced meat, egg, cheese.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:00–1:00; Sat 17:00–23:30; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Cash only; smoking allowed (Tabelog). Queues at peak times, but turnover is quick.

places.cuisine: Tantanmen specialist · Sichuan street-style dan dan with minced meat, garlic chives and bean sprouts · yatai-style shoyu ramen with Sichuan pepper and thin noodles · raw egg, cheese and big cilantro toppings · ¥1,150 with cheese · 13 seats · cash only
places.notes: [Ramen · Sichuan tantanmen on the Nippombashi side] A 13-seat tantanmen shop with a few outdoor seats, dinner only, with queues that move fast. Ask the owner, who will steer you: in October 2026 the advice was to skip the Taiwan, Shanghai and Hong Kong options and order the Sichuan street-style dan dan, with a sharp chili-and-Sichuan-pepper heat over deep umami, under minced meat, garlic chives and bean sprouts. It cost ¥1,150 with cheese. Tame it with a raw egg or cheese, or go all in with extra cilantro. The yatai-style shoyu ramen also carries Sichuan pepper, over thin noodles. Portions are big, so come before you are too full. Cash only, smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Owner-run tantanmen and izakaya counter (reviews); no source names the owner.

anecdotes.text: "The owner informed me that the options from Taiwan, Shanghai, and Hong Kong are not good. So, I ordered the Sichuan Street-style Dan Dan Noodles with cheese. The total came to JPY 1150, tax included." — October 2026.
"I tried the Tabucchan Yatai-style Soy Sauce Ramen. The broth had a nice kick from the Sichuan pepper while still being flavorful, and the noodles were thin." — September 2026.

places.name: 札幌らーめん獅子王 心斎橋店 (Sapporo Ramen Shishio)
places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; miso broth.
places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone and chicken broth, lard, chashu.
places.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Sun 18:00–6:00 (L.O. 5:30); Wed–Thu 18:00–8:00 (L.O. 7:30); Fri, Sat and nights before holidays 18:00–14:00 next day (L.O. 13:30). Closed for cleaning on the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays (Tabelog). Ticket machine at the entrance.
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 2-3-21, NIPPO Tamayachō Kaikan 1F — near Kintetsu Nippombashi
places.cuisine: Sapporo miso ramen ¥1,170 · pork-bone and chicken-wing broth thickened with grated potato · lard cap keeps it piping hot · medium-thick curly yellow noodles · grilled chashu, menma, corn, green onion · ajitama +¥160 · spicy miso · 14-seat counter, open through the night
places.notes: [Ramen · Sapporo miso through the night in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A 14-seat counter serving Sapporo-style miso ramen from 6 pm until morning, and on Friday and Saturday nights until 2 pm the next day. The broth is pork bone and chicken wings simmered long, with miso and a twist: grated potato thickens it to a velvety, potage-like body. A cap of lard keeps it scalding. Medium-thick, curly yellow noodles hold it well, topped with grilled chashu, menma, corn and green onion. The miso ramen was ¥1,170 and an ajitama ¥160 in October 2026. The spicy version isn't very spicy. Buy a ticket at the door. It gets crowded late, but turnover is quick.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog introduction: "Wild yet Mild… The Ultimate Sapporo Miso Ramen Makes Its Debut in Osaka", broth of pork bones and chicken wings, grated potato, medium-thick high-hydration curly noodles.

anecdotes.text: "The miso soup, based on pork and chicken bones, had grated potatoes mixed in, giving it a creamy, velvety texture. The noodles were medium-thick, curly, and had a delightful chewiness." — October 2026, miso ramen ¥1,170, ajitama ¥160.
"A layer of lard on the surface helps retain the heat, keeping the soup at a high temperature… the addition of corn and garlic enhances the aftertaste." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 札幌らーめん獅子王 心斎橋店、大阪市中央区東心斎橋2-3-21 NIPPO玉屋町会館1F、14席(カウンター)、月火日18:00〜翌6:00(L.O.5:30)、水木18:00〜翌8:00(L.O.7:30)、金土祝前日18:00〜翌14:00(L.O.13:30)、第1・第3水曜は清掃のため休み、禁煙、カード・電子マネー可、2016年5月20日開店。店の紹介: ワイルドなのにマイルド、豚骨と鶏ガラ(手羽)を長時間煮込んだスープ、刻み玉ねぎ、すりおろしたじゃがいもでとろみ、中太の多加水ちぢれ麺。2026年の口コミ(9〜10月): 入口の券売機、満席で少し待つ、濃厚でちぢれ麺、椎茸の酢、札幌らしい濃い味噌、ほのかな辛さ、中太麺、ラードで熱々、コーンとにんにく、焼きチャーシュー・メンマ・ねぎ・コーン、深夜2時、半熟玉子の味噌ラーメン、辛いものはあまり辛くない、近鉄日本橋駅近く、味噌ラーメン1,170円、味玉160円。

places.name: Comeconoco Gluten-free Laboratory & Cafe 大阪天満橋店
places.gf_detail: The café calls itself a gluten-free specialist in sweets and bread made from domestic rice flour (「国産米粉を使用した、グルテンフリーなお菓子専門店」). FMGF marks it "Reported to be dedicated gluten-free", with a dedicated GF kitchen space reported, and celiac reviewers (October 2026) praise the sandwiches, croque monsieur and French toast. Confirm when ordering.
places.vegan_detail: Ask. The café menu includes bacon, ham-and-cheese croque monsieur and dairy sweets; no vegan item is described.
places.hours_raw: Eat-in and takeaway Wed–Sat 11:00–17:00; rice-flour baking classes on irregular days (official site).
places.neighborhood: Shimamachi 2-2-3, Sunheim Tenmabashi 101 — between Tenmabashi and Kitahama
places.cuisine: Gluten-free rice-flour café and baking school · croque monsieur lunch set · sandwiches and toasties · French toast plate with bacon · scones, cakes, carrot cake, cream puffs, tarts · afternoon tea · matcha espresso latte · takeaway treats
places.notes: [Café · a gluten-free rice-flour café in Tenmabashi] A small café and baking school near Tenmabashi built entirely around domestic rice flour: gluten-free sweets, bread and a brunch-and-lunch menu that celiac visitors rave about. One called the sandwiches "the best I've ever eaten". Try the croque monsieur lunch set, which a mixed GF and non-GF table loved equally, or the French toast plate with bacon and greens, with a matcha espresso latte. The case holds scones, cakes, carrot cake, cream puffs and tarts to take away, and there is afternoon tea. Small, but turnover is quick. Open Wednesday to Saturday, 11 to 5.

chef_bio.background: A rice-flour sweets café and baking class ("Comeconoco Laboratory Cafe") with an online shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「日本のお米の魅力を発信する、あたらしいスイーツのお店」 (official site).

places.notes: [Mexican · a gluten-friendly taco bar in Honmachibashi] A small Mexican kitchen bar where the menu isn't marked, but much of it is naturally gluten-free thanks to corn tortillas. Celiac reviewers order the nachos ("best I've ever eaten out"), pork, beef and corned-beef tacos, and a gluten-free chocolate cake, with a mango margarita sour or tequila highball. places.cuisine: Okonomiyaki from the house that claims the original "modern-yaki" (with noodles) · modern-yaki ¥1,850 (pork, shrimp, squid) · cheese-tama with potato and mentaiko ¥1,350 · takoyaki, akashiyaki · yakisoba, garlic rice · teppan counter · 94 seats
places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Botejyu's Dotonbori main shop] The 94-seat main shop of Botejyu, which says it has passed down its okonomiyaki and mayonnaise for over 78 years and calls its "modern-yaki" (okonomiyaki layered with noodles) the original. It sits upstairs by the Glico sign, with a live teppan counter. Most customers and staff are now from overseas, and the menus come in about four languages. The okonomiyaki is cooked elsewhere and finished on your table grill with a rich, sweet sauce and mayonnaise. Order the classic modern-yaki with pork, shrimp and squid (¥1,850, August 2026) or the cheese-tama with potato and mentaiko (¥1,350). Portions are big, so start with one each. Regulars note prices have climbed. Tabelog lists vegan options; ask.

places.notes: [Gyoza · Minmin's old-line gyoza house by NGK] The Minami-Sennichimae main shop of Minmin, with a cramped first-floor counter and table floors above. Regulars have been coming back for decades for gyoza and beer. The pan-fried gyoza (¥450) are crisp with crunchy cabbage inside, and a beer set brings gyoza, mapo tofu and a draft for ¥1,600. The shoyu ramen and gyoza set (¥990, September 2026) has a clear amber broth with thin straight noodles, and the sweet-and-sour pork set is generous. Also on the menu: twice-cooked pork, liver with garlic chives and a crab-and-tofu stew. Service is brisk to dry, and staff often speak Chinese among themselves. Handy before or after a show at NGK.

chef_bio.background: Minmin (minminhonten.com); reviewers describe decades of visits (2026).

places.notes: [Ramen · Zundoya's 24-hour Shinsaibashi branch] A 32-seat, round-the-clock Zundoya at the northern end of Shinsaibashi, with a few terrace seats. The chain began in Himeji. You tailor the bowl: thin or curly noodles, back fat from light to extra rich, firmness from soft to very firm. The rich, fatty tonkotsu clings to thin, firm noodles, and with extra back fat it is heavy at 8 am. Load it with table garlic, pickled ginger and pepper. The garlic fried rice is a standout. Lunch, 11 to 4, is set meals only, for example vegetable ramen with a small fried rice for ¥1,400 in October 2026. Buy a ticket at the entrance. Friendly, energetic staff.

chef_bio.background: Zundoya chain (zundouya.com), which an October 2026 reviewer notes began in Himeji.

anecdotes.text: "I chose extra back fat and firm noodles. The broth is a rich tonkotsu with a generous amount of back fat, making it quite heavy. Perhaps I should have opted for regular back fat for breakfast?" — October 2026, just past 8 am.
"You can choose between thin noodles or curly noodles. For the back fat, you can select from light, medium, rich, or extra rich." — October 2026, lunch set ¥1,400.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · Mita Seimenjo's thick-noodle tsukemen by Amza] A 54-seat branch of the Mita Seimenjo tsukemen chain near Amza, open from 10 am to 3 am and busy at lunch. The classic is thick, chewy noodles with a rich dip, and you can upsize free to 500 g. Season with katsuobushi salt or garlic shichimi, and finish with soup-wari. Limited specials rotate: a black-bonito tsukemen with a strong katsuo hit, a niboshi chuka soba (¥1,100, October 2026) so intense it tastes like "liquid niboshi", and in summer a chilled sea-bream shio tsukemen (¥1,340 with everything) and a cold soy-milk tantanmen (¥1,150) heaped with Sichuan pepper. Order by QR code at the table.

places.notes: [Ramen · offal mazesoba on Europe-dōri, round the clock] The Europe-dōri branch of Horumon Ramen 8910, open 24 hours. The draw is the limited spicy horumon mazesoba (¥1,280, October 2026; the large is the same price): thick, curly, chewy noodles in a fiery sauce with offal chunks like a yakiniku restaurant's, plus lots of fried onion. It is much spicier than expected, so stir in an egg. There's also a slightly sweet shoyu ramen (¥1,050) and a spicy kalbi ramen (¥990). Reviews are mixed: several found the regular ramen and beef-bone white soup underwhelming, and it is often quiet. Staff are polite.

anecdotes.text: "The thick, curly noodles have a satisfying chewiness, and the rich spicy sauce is delicious… The Horumon pieces are substantial, almost like what you'd find at a yakiniku restaurant." — October 2026, spicy horumon mazesoba ¥1,280.

places.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog Ramen 100 counter inside Kintetsu Namba station] A 12-seat counter inside the Kintetsu Osaka-Namba ticket gates, named to the Tabelog Ramen OSAKA "100" for 2025. Two clear, beautiful bowls: a free-range-chicken shoyu, oily but not heavy, deep with chicken and a clean finish, and a golden clam-broth ramen. Both come with rare chashu and pork-belly chashu, thick menma, mitsuba, yuzu and caramelised onion. A soft ajitama ramen with grilled chashu rice was ¥1,690 in October 2026, and the plain bowl has crept up to ¥1,150. Food arrives in three to five minutes. The ticket machine is a confusing two-step process (choose, get a QR code, scan and pay cash). If you're not travelling, a ¥180 station admission ticket is refunded as a discount.

places.notes: [Ramen · soy-tonkotsu chuka soba on EDION Namba's ramen floor] One of the shops on "Namba Ramen Ichiza", the 9th-floor ramen street in EDION Namba, and a regular's favourite there. The broth is a soy-sauce tonkotsu, comforting and fragrant, light yet deep for some and surprisingly rich and fatty for others. The shoyu ramen (¥980, June 2026) comes with thin curly noodles, and a fried-rice set adds ¥400. A spicy ramen with ajitama (¥1,150) has a real kick with garlic chives. There's also a curry ramen with big pieces of meat, and a minced-meat ramen with a small rice to mop up. The walls are signed by Yoshimoto comedians. Families come after toy shopping on 7F, and there are high chairs. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Shop on the Namba Ramen Ichiza floor of EDION Namba (ramen-ichiza.edion.com).

places.notes: [Ramen · Kotan's ramen-and-set-meal kitchen under Nippombashi] A newer format from Kotan, the Osaka ramen chain going since 1968: a bright counter-and-table kitchen in Namba Walk by the Nippombashi plaza, mixing the familiar KOTAN ramen with set meals. The shoyu or miso KOTAN ramen (miso ¥820, July 2026) comes with simple, satisfying chashu. Pair it with a mini fried rice or a tenshinhan set, which is unlike the usual Chinese-restaurant version. Gyoza (set ¥500), a chashu-egg set meal with miso soup and pickles, and a stir-fried meat-and-vegetable set suit rice people. In summer there's a bright-red spicy cold ramen with kimchi and smoked egg. One regular has been more than 30 times.

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night Sichuan ramen in a Sōemonchō alley] Opened in December 2025 in a back alley off Sōemon-dōri: a 13-seat, two-floor shop that runs from 9 pm into the morning and is made for a post-drinks bowl. The signature Sichuan ramen (¥1,000) has a pleasantly spicy, rich broth over house-made thin noodles, almost somen-like, under a big heap of crunchy greens. Season it with garlic and lemon. A black shoyu ramen and a strong soy-sauce shoyu are the alternatives, and the fried rice (kimchi, or garlic and pepper) is good. Hours can slip: one October visitor arrived to find it opening late and out of Sichuan ramen. The stiff door is a known quirk. Cash only.

places.gf_detail: Ask. The takoyaki is made with rice flour (May 2026), but yakisoba and other dishes are not described as gluten-free and there is no gluten-free statement.
places.vegan_detail: Vegan versions of Osaka dishes. The rice-flour takoyaki uses konjac instead of octopus (May 2026), a summer chilled shio ramen was "made without any animal products or broth" (June 2025), and there is vegan chocolate ice cream (June 2026). Tabelog lists vegan and vegetarian options. Two 2026 reviewers call it a vegan café, but whether everything is vegan is not stated, so ask.

places.cuisine: Travel-themed café-bar with veganised Osaka food · rice-flour takoyaki with konjac instead of octopus (with salad and soup) · vegan yakisoba · summer vegan chilled shio ramen with fried vegetables ¥1,780 · vegan chocolate ice cream ¥650 · drinks · ~40 seats · cashless
places.notes: [Café · veganised Osaka food in the Kuidaore Building] A modern, roomy café-bar on the ground floor of the Nakaza Kuidaore Building, on Dotonbori's main drag, that pitches itself as a travel base and serves Osaka classics in vegan form. The takoyaki is made with rice flour and konjac in place of octopus, which the menu doesn't spell out, and comes as a set with salad and soup. Summer 2025 brought a chilled shio ramen made without animal products, topped with fried eggplant, okra and pumpkin, tomato and pickled ginger (¥1,780). A friend with a dairy allergy was delighted with the vegan chocolate ice cream (¥650). Prices are steep and it is often quiet. Multilingual, cashless, QR ordering.

places.notes: [Okonomiyaki · fluffy okonomiyaki in Hōzenji Yokochō] A 26-seat okonomiyaki shop tucked into an alley of Hōzenji Yokochō, with queues of mostly overseas visitors, so book or arrive at opening. The batter is famously fluffy ("the fluffiest okonomiyaki I've ever had"). The signature combination is beef tendon, green onion and konnyaku, rich and generous, while the mixed pork, squid and shrimp is lighter. Start with teppan plates like grilled squid with salt and lemon or chicken thigh with ponzu. Negi-tonpei, modern-yaki and a butter-mentaiko yakisoba round it out. Ingredients are big, and service is skilled and quick. Closed Tuesdays; lunch at weekends only.

places.cuisine: Chicken-based rich shoyu chuka soba ¥980 with pork-belly and rare roast chashu · shio and shoyu chicken paitan · spicy chicken paitan (large ¥1,350) · summer chilled bonito-kombu-water ramen ¥1,100 · grilled chicken yukke rice bowl ¥500 · seasoned egg ¥200
places.notes: [Ramen · chicken shoyu and paitan on EDION's ramen floor] A 23-seat shop on Namba Ramen Ichiza, EDION Namba's 9th-floor ramen street, since April 2025. The chuka soba (¥980, October 2026) is a chicken-based, rich shoyu that hits hard on umami and salt, with smooth, slightly thin straight noodles, a slice of pork belly and one of rare roast. There are chicken paitans in shio and shoyu (one regular found the shio lighter than before), a spicy paitan, and in summer a chilled ramen in bonito and thick, sticky kombu water. Add the chicken yukke rice bowl (¥500). It is busier than its neighbours in the evening, often with overseas visitors.

"When I tried to scoop up the soup, it was so thick that I couldn't get any! (laughs) It wasn't thick from fat, but rather from the sticky texture of the kombu." — September 2026, chilled bonito-kombu ramen.

places.cuisine: Tokyo Yokohama-style iekei since 1999 · rich tonkotsu-shoyu from domestic pork bones and chicken · thick firm noodles · spinach and nori · ajitama ramen with nori and small rice ¥1,250 · free rice (large OK) · table garlic and ginger · limited "Musajirō" Jirō-style ¥1,300 · chilled tonkotsu (summer) · 32 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · Kichijōji's iekei on EDION's ramen floor] The Namba branch of Kichijoji Musashiya, an iekei shop founded in Kichijōji, Tokyo, in 1999 to bring the then-rare Yokohama style to the west of Tokyo. It sits on EDION Namba's 9th-floor ramen street. The broth is rich tonkotsu shoyu made, the shop says, with an extraordinary amount of domestic pork bones and chicken carcasses. It comes over thick, firm noodles with spinach in place of green onion, plus nori, and garlic and ginger on the table. Rice is free, in a large size if you like. An ajitama ramen with nori and small rice was ¥1,250 in October 2026. A limited "Musajirō" Jirō-style bowl (¥1,300) piles on vegetables, back fat and garlic. Reviewers call it consistent, classic iekei, if not remarkable.

anecdotes.text: "Kichijoji Musashiya was established on May 13, 1999, in Kichijoji, Tokyo. The restaurant started with the desire to deliver the then-rare Yokohama-style ramen to many customers." — October 2026, ajitama ramen with nori and small rice ¥1,250.
"The broth had a rich flavor typical of the house style, and there were plenty of toppings like spinach and seaweed. With garlic and ginger available on the table." — August 2026.

places.cuisine: Jinrui Mina Menrui spin-off · shellfish-broth ramen with a big hit of salt and umami · sansho-oil ramen ¥1,200 · recommended curry ramen · mazesoba with bonito · limited cold ramen with ume, shiso and grated yam ¥1,280 (10 a day) · medium-thick curly whole-wheat noodles · mentaiko rice bowl
places.notes: [Ramen · a Jinrui Mina Menrui spin-off in Amerikamura] A newer shop in Amemura, since October 2025, from the people behind Osaka's Jinrui Mina Menrui (one reviewer credits its founder, "UNCHI"), open to 11 pm. Bowls carry lucky-god names such as Daikokuten and Benzaiten. The shellfish-broth ramen hits with salt and umami at once, over smooth, medium-thick curly whole-wheat noodles; add black pepper halfway. There's also a sansho-oil ramen (¥1,200) with a clear numbing note and an oversized sheet of nori, a curry ramen the shop recommends, a mazesoba under bonito flakes, and in summer a cold ramen in light dashi with ume, pickled turnip, shiso and grated yam (¥1,280, 10 bowls a day). At weekday lunch, large noodles and rice are free. Prices run high, and two reviewers found the service brusque.

chef_bio.background: Produced by the team behind Jinrui Mina Menrui ("Ramen produced by Humanity's Noodle UNCHI", July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the Benzaiten (Shellfish Broth Ramen). The broth was amazing! The saltiness and umami hit me at once! The noodles were medium-thick, curly, and made with whole wheat flour." — June 2026, weekday lunch.
"They only serve 10 bowls a day… The broth is a light Japanese dashi, complemented by the tanginess of pickled plum and marinated turnip." — August 2026, limited cold ramen ¥1,280.

places.notes: [Tsukemen · Kyoto-born rich tsukemen on EDION's ramen floor] A branch of Menya Takei, a tsukemen shop with its main branch in Kyoto, on EDION Namba's 9th-floor ramen street, and one regular's favourite there. The rich chicken-and-pork-bone dip, blended with seafood, is thick without being too salty or greasy. It clings to slightly firm, flat, thick and chewy noodles: even the small is 330 g, and the large is 450 g. Staff will reheat the dip. Rich tsukemen runs about ¥1,200–1,280, and the special with ajitama was ¥1,540 in October 2026. There's also a rich chuka soba (¥1,150) and a spicy topping (¥150). One diner likened it to a Kansai take on Noroshi. Another found it just normally good for the price, and a regular felt the noodles had softened lately. Open all afternoon.

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a thick and flavorful seafood and pork bone mix, paired with slightly firm, flat, thick noodles… The soup was rich without being overly salty or greasy, which is quite rare to find." — October 2026, rich chuka soba ¥1,150.

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu shoyu in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small counter of about eight seats, run by one person and open from 10 pm to 7:30 am. The rich tonkotsu shoyu (¥1,300, October 2026) bursts with flavour yet finishes clean. A reviewer credits a Kyoto aged soy sauce for bringing out the pork's sweetness. The fried rice comes only in a large size. Service can be curt, and it is pricey for ramen, but there are few bowls this good at 5 am.

places.notes: [Chinese · Sōemonchō's refined Sichuan kitchen] A 20-seat Sichuan restaurant with a long counter and tables at the back, named to Tabelog's Chinese WEST "100" in 2021 and run by a small team. One reviewer describes the chef as a disciple of Chen Kenmin. The tantanmen, in soup or dry, is the most popular dish, refined and milder than expected, so ask for it spicier. The scallop fried rice (¥1,000), seen on TV, is moist yet fluffy, and fried rice comes with shrimp, crab or vegetables too, in half portions alongside any dish. The salt seafood stir-fry of shrimp and squid (¥1,800) impressed one diner. Gyoza, yurinchi and a gentle green-onion ramen to finish are also on offer. Dinner only, 6 to 10 pm, and always full.

places.notes: [Ramen · beef-bone ramen on EDION's ramen floor] A 10-seat beef-bone ramen shop on EDION Namba's 9th-floor ramen street, since December 2025, with a minotaur on display. The special beef-bone white soup (¥1,000, October 2026) is cloudy, creamy and robustly beefy without heaviness. It comes over slightly flat noodles with roast beef, pea shoots, baby corn and red cabbage sprouts. Regulars also rave about the clear beef broth, with noodles of just the right thickness and firmness. The golden niboshi version (¥1,080) layers sardine over beef. A black beef-bone curry comes with excellent white rice. Until 9 pm, extra noodles are free; one diner went five rounds. A voluble owner runs the kitchen.

chef_bio.background: A shop on the Namba Ramen Ichiza floor (namba-ramen-ichiza.com); no source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "Taking a sip of the cloudy broth, I immediately tasted the robust flavor of beef! It has a unique richness that sets it apart from pork or chicken broth—creamy yet not too heavy." — October 2026, special beef-bone white soup ¥1,000.
"The noodles were slightly firm, which I personally enjoyed. I ordered extra noodles five times, and they happily accommodated me with a smile!" — August 2026.

places.name: 薬膳スパイスカレー＆グルテンフリーバル Spys Oasis
places.gf_detail: The shop describes itself as serving gluten-free food and drinks, and explains on its site that it does not use gluten (「グルテンは使わないんです」). Tabelog's introduction says "completely gluten-free dishes and drinks", and a September 2026 reviewer reports "all products are 100% gluten-free", with no dairy or white sugar. Gluten-free drinks are served even at the bar, for example a GF Red Eye. Tabelog notes allergy information is available. The shop's stated reason is health rather than celiac safety, and no cross-contact controls are described, so confirm if you are celiac.
places.vegan_detail: A separate vegan-and-gluten-free curry line on the official menu: root-vegetable curry, soy-mince and red-pepper salsa curry, and a pumpkin, banana, mango, corn and chickpea curry (¥1,700 each, ¥1,800 for two, ¥1,900 for three), with vegan toppings. The house three-curry set contains chicken, pork and mackerel, and the soup is made with chicken.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Wed, Fri–Sat: lunch 11:30–15:00, bar 18:00–24:00 (one-drink minimum); Sun and holidays 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00; closed Thursdays; changes on social media (official site). Online booking only, no phone reservations (official site).
places.neighborhood: Namba 1-5-8, a few minutes south of Dotonbori
places.cuisine: Yakuzen (medicinal-herb) spice curry, gluten-free · three-curry "san-mi ittai" set: soy-milk tomato chicken, black-sesame red-miso pork-hijiki keema, mackerel and lotus-root green curry ¥1,600–3,880 · vegan curry line ¥1,700–1,900 · basmati and 15-grain rice · roast chicken leg ¥1,280 · GF bar drinks and natural wine · 14 seats
places.notes: [Curry · gluten-free yakuzen spice curry by Dotonbori] A 14-seat curry café and evening bar run on a "food as medicine" concept by a yakuzen (medicinal-cooking) specialist. Everything is gluten-free by the shop's own account. The signature is three curries to mix: a soy-milk, onion, tomato and ginger chicken-breast curry; a black-sesame and red-miso pork-and-hijiki keema; and a mackerel and lotus-root "green Popeye" curry. Each is tangy and spiced, and they come together into one flavour when mixed. They sit over basmati and 15-grain rice (Simple ¥1,600; Standard ¥2,000 with soup, salad and toppings). A separate vegan line covers root-vegetable, soy-mince salsa and tropical chickpea curries. At night it becomes a bar with GF drinks, natural wine and tapas. English menu; book online.

chef_bio.background: Official site: yakuzen spice curry made by a yakuzen meister (薬膳マイスター), on the principle 医食同源 ("food and medicine share one source").

places.cuisine: Egyptian café and shisha bar · koshari · ta'ameya (falafel) · hummus with pita · garlicky molokhia soup · shish tawook chicken plate ~¥1,600–1,800 · kahk and baklava · hibiscus juice, mint tea · shisha ¥2,200 · halal options · dance-show events
places.notes: [Middle Eastern · an Egyptian café and shisha bar in Amemura] A moody, Egyptian-styled café on the 3rd floor of a building in Amerikamura that serves lunch and runs as a shisha bar at night, with occasional dance shows. Staff explain the dishes and share stories about Egypt. Order koshari, the national dish of rice, macaroni and lentils in tomato sauce under crisp fried onions, with garlic vinegar and chili oil to season. There's also ta'ameya (Egyptian falafel), hummus with pita, a rich, garlicky molokhia soup, and shish tawook chicken plates (about ¥1,600–1,800). Finish with baklava or kahk and hibiscus juice or mint tea. Tabelog lists vegan, vegetarian and halal options. Opening days vary, so check Instagram or book. On event nights, food can take an hour.

chef_bio.background: An Egyptian restaurant and shisha café; operating days announced on Instagram (Tabelog remarks). No source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered koshari, Egypt's national dish… It consists of rice, macaroni, and lentils topped with tomato sauce. The generous amount of crispy fried onions added a delightful crunch." — September 2026.

"We ordered: Koshari, Hummus with Pita Bread, Molokhia Soup, Ta'ameya Falafel, Kahk, Baklava, Hibiscus Juice… The staff carefully explained each dish and shared interesting facts about Egypt." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Sweets · Namba's famous crêpes and galettes] A 50-seat French crêperie up steep stairs just south of Dotonbori, named to Tabelog's Sweets WEST "100" in 2023 and 2026, with a takeout line downstairs. The crêpes, made with French flour, Échiré butter and salt, are crisp at the edge and chewy inside. The plain Échiré butter and sugar is the one regulars call the best they've had. At lunch, try a daily galette from the blackboard, say beef stew over mashed potato and cheese, or tandoori chicken, in the crêperie lunch (¥2,200, October 2026). There's also a milk-jam crêpe set with vanilla gelato (¥1,480), quiche and Mont Blanc. The takeout queue is about 10 minutes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Selected for Tabelog Sweets WEST "100" 2023 and 2026; Tabelog introduction: French flour, Échiré butter and salt.

anecdotes.text: "Both were perfectly crispy and fragrant, and the batter itself was outstanding! The galette had beef stew underneath, with mashed potatoes and cheese hidden between the layers." — October 2026, crêperie lunch ¥2,200, cash only.
"I had a crepe with Échiré butter and sugar. The takeout line took about 10 minutes… The outside was crispy while the inside was chewy and moist." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura in the Namba Walk mall] A roomy Kamukura in the Namba Walk underground mall, since 2024, with tables that suit solo diners and tablet ordering. The broth is the chain's soy-based soup, light but deep with the sweetness of napa cabbage. The vegetable-packed ramen is the regulars' choice, topped up with the garlic chives at the counter. Autumn 2026 brought a limited hot-and-sour ramen, lighter than the usual thick suan-la, just right for some and refreshing for others. A ramen, gyoza, fried rice and beer set makes a hearty lunch.

places.notes: [Yakitori · Kyushu-style yakitori and kamameshi by Namba station] A red-lantern izakaya in a back alley by Namba Station, open from 5 pm to 4 am, part of the SASAYA group. Charcoal-grilled Kyushu-style yakitori comes as shareable pieces rather than skewers: an assorted three kinds is ¥1,320 (April 2026), alongside grilled vegetables (¥1,078) and fried mehikari (¥858). Finish with kamameshi, rice cooked to order in an iron pot, like the chicken soboro and burdock, so order it early. Ordering is by LINE. The upstairs can get smoky from the grill, and there's a pleasant terrace. Note the name: Tabelog lists it as Nakamoto, while several 2026 reviews call it "Yakitori to Kamameshi Gotchin".

places.notes: [Chinese · malatang with a beef-bone white broth in Nippombashi] A clean, 20-seat malatang shop a few minutes from Nippombashi, relaxed enough when reviewers came that you can take your time at the ingredient case. The difference is the broth: beef bone, and the original white version is rich enough at zero spice to taste like ramen soup. Vegetables soaked in it, broccoli especially, are the reviewers' pick. Spice runs from 0 up to a numbing level 3 at least, and chili oil comes on the side. One mala fan ranks it third of 19 places tried. Spend over ¥1,000, as most do, and a can from the fridge is free. The aroma inside takes a minute to get used to.

places.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chashu, tonkotsu ramen, kara-age; fish flakes on the condiment shelf.
places.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:30 and 17:00–5:00 (Tabelog). Tonkotsu ramen only from 22:00 (October 2026 reviews). Opened 20 September 2026. Digital ticket machine; Tabelog lists QR payments (no e-money), but in September 2026 electronic payment was not yet working and a reviewer had to pay cash.

places.cuisine: Abura-soba ¥850 on thick, curly house-made noodles · all-toppings abura-soba · mazesoba ¥1,000 · Taiwanese mazesoba · from 22:00, a light, creamy tonkotsu ramen ¥900 and a meat-loaded version ¥1,100 · set A (rice and kara-age) +¥300 · vinegar, chili oil, garlic, spicy miso on the table
places.notes: [Ramen · late-night abura-soba in Amemura] A new Roman shop, opened on 20 September 2026 among the Amerika-mura live houses and open until 5 am. Roman is an Osaka brand that began in Morinomiya in 2022. The abura-soba (¥850) is the plain, steady kind, on thick, curly house-made noodles cut short enough to slurp. Reviewers douse it in vinegar and chili oil, add garlic or kimchi, and find it not greasy at all. The mazesoba (¥1,000) comes with more sauce than expected and a strong soy edge, and there is a Taiwanese mazesoba. After 10 pm the shop adds something the name doesn't promise: a smooth, milky tonkotsu ramen on thin straight noodles (¥900; ¥1,100 piled with chashu), creamy but light enough for that hour. You buy a ticket at the machine; about three tables and eight counter seats.

chef_bio.background: The Roman brand started in Morinomiya, Osaka, in 2022 (October 2026 review); new Kobe Motomachi and Kishiwada shops opened the month before this one (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Abura-soba and mazesoba; tonkotsu ramen late at night.

anecdotes.text: "The thick, curly noodles coated in flavor are short enough to slurp easily… although it's called Abura-soba, it's not greasy at all." — September 2026.
"While specializing in Abura-soba and Mazesoba, this Amemura location also offers Tonkotsu ramen starting at 10 PM." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Korean · Japanese-Korean sundubu in Namba Walk] A calm, 17-seat sundubu shop in the Namba Walk underground mall, by Nippombashi Station, here for about a year by autumn 2026. The soft-tofu stew is rich and sweet beneath the heat. Spice runs from 1 to 4, with 2 as standard. Several reviewers found 3 easy going, and 1 not spicy at all. Sets come with rice and three small sides, and a scoop of lychee sorbet arrives at the end. The Namba-only sundubu ramen puts noodles in the stew (one visitor added rice for ¥100), though one reviewer compared the noodles to boiled dried noodles rather than real ramen. Other picks are the grilled-pork sundubu with clams and minced meat, grilled-cheese sundubu ramen, and Wakan herb cold noodles. The manager runs the floor attentively; you buy a ticket at the entrance. Tabelog spells the name "Juraku"; the kana じゅろく reads Juroku.

chef_bio.origin: Open about a year as of September 2026 (review)
chef_bio.background: Japanese-Korean (wakan) sundubu specialist; "なんば別邸" branch name (Tabelog). A reviewer has seen it on TV recently (October 2026).

places.cuisine: Kishu Wakayama ramen ¥950 + tax, light or rich, and an "aged" version · shrimp tsukemen · seasonal Japanese-style tororo cold ramen ¥1,210 · half-portion kara-age · thin noodles · 20 seats (12 counter) · open until 5–6 am
places.notes: [Ramen · Wakayama-style ramen until dawn on Dotonbori] A Wakayama-style ramen shop by the Sōemonchō end of Dotonbori, open from 9 am until 5 am (6 am on Fridays, Saturdays and the night before a holiday), full of tourists from home and abroad. The Kishu Wakayama ramen (¥950 before tax, September 2026) is a soy-tonkotsu bowl on thin noodles. There's a light option, a rich one, and an "aged" ramen, which one July 2026 reviewer found just right in flavor and fat as an after-drinks bowl. Also on the menu: a shrimp-heavy tsukemen, and in September a limited Japanese-style tororo cold ramen (¥1,210) with chicken chashu and a tempura egg on chilled thin noodles. Opinions split in autumn 2026. One returning visitor found the broth weak and lukewarm, while another drank every drop. Watch the menu: the big number is before tax. You pay on the way out.

places.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles under the mapo tofu; mazesoba sauce is soy-based.
places.vegan_detail: The shop's own Tabelog text says it offers vegetarian and halal menu options ("please feel free to ask our staff"), and Tabelog tags it "Offering vegan menu". No review describes a vegetarian or vegan bowl, so ask what is in the mapo sauce and broth.
places.hours_raw: Mon–Thu and the day before or after a public holiday 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and 18:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); Fri–Sun 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–4:00 (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted. No cover charge.
places.neighborhood: Higashi-Shinsaibashi 1-15-22, Daiichi KS Bldg B1F — about 2 min from Shinsaibashi and Nagahoribashi Stns
places.cuisine: Mapo tofu ramen, with made-to-order mapo over chewy medium-thick noodles · spicy noodle soup · mapo rice bowl · yurinchi · monthly limited bowls (October 2026: seafood and meat-miso mazesoba ¥1,300; July 2026: explosive-garlic mapo ramen ¥1,500; summer: chilled basil mapo ramen) · saba-dashi rice ¥300 · vegetarian and halal options on request · 26 seats
places.notes: [Ramen · mapo tofu ramen under Higashi-Shinsaibashi] The Shinsaibashi branch of a mapo-tofu-ramen specialist from Naramachi, Nara, in a calm, chic basement with a long counter, tables and a projector. It is open until 4 am Friday to Sunday. The signature is mapo tofu ladled hot over the noodles. The Nara shop describes made-to-order mapo on smooth, chewy medium-thick noodles, and one reviewer ended up sweating and ordering rice for the leftover sauce. A limited bowl changes through the year. October 2026 brought a seafood and meat-miso mazesoba (¥1,300) with egg yolk, fish powder, chives and bean sprouts on thick, chewy noodles. Summer had a chilled basil mapo ramen. Finish with saba-dashi rice (¥300). The shop says it offers vegetarian and halal options; ask the staff. One October 2026 visitor found it empty at Friday lunch and had to call for service.

chef_bio.origin: Main shop: Naramachi, Nara (official site); the Shinsaibashi ramen uses mapo tofu from the main shop (August 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Tabelog listing: "Celebrating 6 Years of Mapo Tofu and Noodles Crafted by Master Chefs!" The official site lists only the Naramachi main shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: The shop says it wants the dish to contribute to society by offering vegetarian and halal menu options (Tabelog).

places.notes: [Café · Mediterranean breakfast-to-midnight on the Dotonbori River] A bright café-restaurant on the ground floor of S-Front Dotonbori, opened July 2025. A riverside terrace (dogs welcome) is the landmark, and it runs from a 7 am breakfast to a late bar. The menu is Middle Eastern and Mediterranean, and the shop says it covers vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free diners; tell them when you book. The reviewed vegan plate is the domestic-corn tartine on rye bread, with sweet charred corn, hummus, avocado, tomato and marinated onions. One September 2026 diner found that nothing felt missing. Falafel pita sandwiches and grilled-chicken shawarma lead at lunch. Breakfast runs to English breakfast, Turkish eggs and a smoked-salmon bagel. The coffee is roasted in-house. English menu and English-speaking staff.

chef_bio.background: Shop text (Tabelog): a barista roasts small batches of beans in-house, including Ethiopian and Colombian; private parties for up to 60.
chef_bio.specialty: Middle Eastern and Mediterranean dishes; breakfast; house-roasted coffee.

anecdotes.text: "It paired well with the creamy hummus and avocado, and even though it's a vegan dish, I didn't feel like anything was missing." — September 2026, domestic corn tartine.
"The 'Falafel Pita Sandwich' was filled with crispy, fluffy falafel, perfectly balanced with spices and vegetables." — August 2026.

places.notes: [Curry · halal Pakistani biryani under Shinsaibashi-suji] A basement Pakistani and Arab kitchen by Shinsaibashi Station that calls itself a halal restaurant, with halal wagyu on its own site. Tabelog has listed it among its 100 best for curry (2019–2020) and Asian/ethnic food (2022–2024). Biryani is what it's known for: ¥1,600 à la carte, or a huge ¥1,000 lunch plate with a drink (October 2026). Vegetarians have real choices: an eggplant-and-potato baingan aloo (¥1,200), the potato samosa (¥800), and a falafel set with hummus and Arabic pickles (¥2,000). The spinach-heavy palak paneer has cheese, and nobody says whether ghee is used, so vegans should ask. Tables fill with visitors from around the world. Closed Thursdays.

places.notes: [Café · Kitahorie chopped-salad shop with vegan dressings] A wood-and-houseplant chopped-salad café in Kitahorie, open since 2017, with sofas and a dog-friendly terrace, three minutes from Yotsubashi. Salads are chopped to order with your choice of toppings. Every house dressing is vegan and additive-free, made without white sugar, eggs, dairy or honey (shop text), and the coconut-lemon oil dressing is refreshing in summer. The signature bowls carry roast beef, salmon, egg or herb chicken, so vegans should build their own. Sweets include a gluten-free lemon cake with pistachio and vegan chocolate-chip cookies, and lattes come with soy, oat or almond milk. There's also a breakfast plate, herb-chicken rice bowls and gapao rice. Order at the counter; salads to go.

chef_bio.philosophy: Additive-free, plant-based dressings; fresh vegetables sourced daily from around Japan (shop text).

places.notes: [Turkish · halal-ingredient Turkish café upstairs in Kitahorie] A clean, stylish second-floor Turkish café and restaurant in Kitahorie, opened April 2024. The cooking is by a chef from Turkey, who is friendly and fluent in Japanese, per reviewers. The shop cooks with halal ingredients and says it caters to vegetarians, and reviewers keep praising the chickpea falafel and the hummus in the mezze platter. Lunch is good value: a ¥1,200 chicken-kebab set with salad, a creamy tomato-and-bean soup and butter rice. The ¥4,500 course runs through mezze, soup, soft Turkish bread, chicken and lamb kebabs, and baklava with Turkish ice cream. Turkish beer and red wine are poured too. Closed Wednesdays.

places.cuisine: Kurobuta tonkotsu from Yukuhashi, Fukuoka · Kurobuta ramen ¥980 in a frothy, "cappuccino" broth · chashu ramen · B set (rice and three kara-age) ¥460 · grilled gyoza · fried rice · thin straight noodles, firmness on request · pickled mustard greens and red ginger on the table
places.notes: [Ramen · Yukuhashi kurobuta tonkotsu on the EDION 9F ramen floor] The Namba Ramen Ichiza branch of Kanadaya, a tonkotsu shop from Yukuhashi in Fukuoka. Its Kurobuta ramen (¥980, October 2026) comes in a thick, creamy broth whipped to a fine foam that reviewers compare to a cappuccino. One reviewer credits that to kurobuta bones simmered for over 20 hours. It's rich but not funky, on thin straight noodles you can order firm. Toppings are three large charred slices of chashu, kikurage, green onion and a big sheet of nori, and pickled mustard greens and red ginger sit on the table. Add the B set (rice and three kara-age, ¥460) or grilled gyoza. One reviewer rates it thicker than Ichiran or Ippudo. It's often quiet before noon, a rare hearty tonkotsu in Namba with no line.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 7 June 2019 (Tabelog); the brand began in Yukuhashi, Fukuoka (reviews)
chef_bio.background: Kanadaya; reviewers have also eaten at its Yukuhashi main shop and Nishinomiya branch.

places.notes: [Ramen · Sendai abura-soba on the EDION 9F ramen floor] An abura-soba shop from Sendai that opened on the Namba Ramen Ichiza floor in December 2025. The original Sendai abura-soba (¥1,150) is mild on its own: chewy medium-thick noodles in a light sauce, under grilled "toro" meat soft enough to melt, half an egg, green onion and nori. You build it yourself with the vinegar and chili oil the sign tells you to add (twice), plus pepper or Sichuan pepper. Beyond it are a punchy G-style bowl with pork fat and garlic, a Taiwanese mazesoba (¥1,150), a rich two-cheese mazesoba with egg yolk (¥1,200) and a tsukimi abura-soba with tororo (¥950). Summer brought a chilled soy-milk tantan mazesoba. There's also a clear Date's salt ramen. Mix the leftover sauce with rice (¥100), or add beef-tongue curry (¥400). Spacious, clean, counter and tables.

places.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan on the EDION 9F ramen floor] A 39-seat chicken-paitan shop in the POPUP Ramen space of Namba Ramen Ichiza, busy from opening. The Miyako ramen (¥930, September 2026) is a light chicken-paitan shoyu with a punch of back fat and pepper on thin noodles, and one reviewer was reminded of Tenkaippin. There's a richer version, plus a spicy miso (¥970) that starts as miso and turns hotter as you stir in the garlicky chili paste. A chicken-paitan shio has a yuzu-like citrus note, and the meat-special ramen carries three kinds of house chashu. Summer brought chilled tantanmen and hiyashi chuka (¥1,100). The rice sets are cheap add-ons: aburi chashu mayo (¥430) or mini fried rice (¥400). Family-friendly, with a kids menu.

places.notes: [Ramen · Amemura's original niboshi tsukemen] Suzume's 12-seat counter in Amerika-mura has been pouring tsukemen since 2010, and people still queue outside. The dipping broth is niboshi-based but smooth and deep. One reviewer, back after 15 years in Tokyo, still calls it the original taste of tsukemen. It's rich with seafood umami, for thick, chewy noodles you can have at 200 g or 300 g for the same price. The cult order is the spicy tsukemen (¥1,000), with heat levels; level 2 is rich rather than fierce. Swap in the red, chili-infused noodles for ¥30. The special (¥1,300) adds thick, tender chashu. Mix, taste, then add vinegar and chili oil. Some long-time regulars feel it isn't quite what it was. Cash only.

places.notes: [Korean · yukgaejang noodles behind Hotel Royal Classic] A 10-seat Korean lunch counter in Ura-Namba, on the street behind Hotel Royal Classic Osaka, open since 2020 and often with a line. Everyone orders the yukgaejang noodles (¥1,200, October 2026): a spicy-sweet beef soup packed with chunky meat and vegetables on thin noodles, hot enough to make you sweat. Add a soft-boiled egg to cool your tongue. The set adds a grilled rare harami rice bowl that some think beats the noodles. The small size is bigger than it looks, and you can tip the leftover rice into the soup. Korean cold noodles suit the spice-shy. Cash only, and smoking is allowed.

places.cuisine: Wagyu ramen served course-style · Osaka wagyu ramen 100 g ¥3,900, 250 g ¥6,900, 450 g ¥10,900 · chicken-bone and flying-fish (ago) shoyu broth · medium-thin wavy noodles from Taiyo Seimenjo · an ago-dashi starter with gold leaf · grilled flying fish ground to powder at the table · wagyu finished on a small teppan
places.notes: [Ramen · course-style wagyu ramen in Nippombashi] A new evening ramen counter that opened on 29 June 2026 in the former Men no Hiromiya space by Nippombashi. It is a new concept from the Dotonbori tonkatsu shop "Ganso 5cm Katsu Don" (review), and the price matches the show: ¥3,900 for 100 g of wagyu, up to ¥10,900 for 450 g. It runs like a little course. A flying-fish dashi with gold leaf comes first. Then a grilled flying fish is cut with scissors and ground into powder in a mortar, and the chef adds it to your bowl. The ramen is a low-viscosity chicken-bone and flying-fish shoyu, light and smooth with a mild seafood sweetness, on chewy medium-thin wavy noodles from Taiyo Seimenjo. The seasoned wagyu flank arrives on a small teppan over a burner so you can cook it to your liking. Only one review so far (July 2026).

chef_bio.background: A new concept from "Ganso 5cm Katsu Don Osaka Tonkatsu" in Dotonbori (July 2026 review); the review gives the name as "CHIYOMATSU'S OSAKA WAGYU RAMEN".

"The wagyu is served on a teppan heated with solid fuel, allowing you to enjoy it at your preferred doneness." — July 2026.

places.cuisine: Chinese, Tabelog 100 (Chinese WEST 2021, 2023, 2024) · yodare chicken piled with cilantro in a heavy sesame-chili sauce · mapo tofu bubbling in a clay pot, as a lunch set · dan dan noodles · spicy chicken · xiao long bao · bean-sprout yakisoba with yellow chives · lunch sets with soup, sides, almond jelly and rice refills · 48 seats
places.notes: [Chinese · Tabelog 100 yodare chicken and mapo in a Shinsaibashi basement] A 48-seat basement Chinese restaurant off Shinsaibashi-suji, on Tabelog's Chinese 100 list in 2021, 2023 and 2024, and the lunch line proves it. The dish everyone orders is yodare chicken, buried under cilantro in a sesame-thick, spicy sauce you toss like a salad; ask for green onion if you don't like cilantro. The mapo tofu arrives bubbling in a clay pot, authentic and properly spicy. The dan dan noodles are rich. Lunch sets come with egg-drop soup, side dishes good enough to be mains, almond jelly and free rice refills. Go after 2 pm to skip the queue. Dinner adds xiao long bao, spicy chicken and water spinach (draft beer is ¥950), and booking is wise.

"Since it comes with cilantro, if you're not a fan, you can ask to switch it for green onions… To finish off, the Mapo Tofu was served bubbling in a clay pot—absolutely the best." — October 2026.

places.notes: [Set meals · fermented-food lunch on Orange Street] A roomy set-meal café among the clothing shops of Horie's Orange Street, built around fermented food. The shop says it uses pesticide-free, additive-free ingredients and handmade or traditionally made seasonings. Most people order the fermented kara-age set, crisp outside and remarkably moist inside, with five small sides. For a meat-free lunch there's the healthy fermented vegetable set, with fragrant miso soup and fermented-enzyme brown rice that turns sweet as you chew (July 2026); ask whether the miso soup uses fish stock. There's also a fried mackerel set, plus fermented shakes and seasonal enzyme juices. Order on the touch panel. It gets busy at lunch, so come early or book.

chef_bio.background: Official site: fermented dishes that are good for the body; pesticide-free, additive-free ingredients with handmade or traditionally made seasonings (2023 price-change notice).
chef_bio.philosophy: Food made with "the power of nature" through fermentation (official site).

anecdotes.text: "I placed my order through a touch panel, choosing the Healthy Fermented Vegetable Set Meal… I appreciated the healthy option, even though it didn't include any meat." — July 2026.
"Thanks to fermentation, the meat is moist and juicy, with flavors locked in tightly." — July 2026, fermented kara-age set.

places.cuisine: Specialty-coffee café in a hotel lobby · lunch plates with organic and vegan deli · additive-free baked goods daily, seasonal carrot cake · rice-flour canelé · weekend rice-flour French toast (peach and Earl Grey, summer 2026) · banana caramel salt muffin · eggs Benedict ¥1,800 · 33 seats on two floors, outlets
places.notes: [Café · hotel-lobby coffee with vegan bakes by Nagahoribashi] The ground-floor café of HOTEL MORNING BOX, a minute from Nagahoribashi and calm even at weekends. It has two floors of tables and sofas, plus counters with outlets where people work and take calls. The shop lists organic and vegan deli options at lunch, and reviewers mention a range of vegan baked goods. The bakes are additive-free and change daily. The cinnamon carrot cake is the Instagram favourite, and the canelé is made with rice flour. Weekends bring a rice-flour French toast; the summer 2026 version had a whole peach and Earl Grey, with mascarpone, so it isn't vegan. Breakfast includes an eggs Benedict (¥1,800) that one guest found more ham-and-eggs. Coffee is the specialty, served from 8 am to 10:30 pm.

places.notes: [Café · high-protein bowls in Kitahorie] A small healthy-bowl café in Kitahorie, three minutes from Nishi-Ohashi, popular with gym-goers and dog owners (it even sells jerky for dogs). Every bowl lists calories and macros. You choose from six base concepts, one of them "Healthy & high-protein for vegans" (shop text), then customize the toppings and dressing. The house PROTEIN LAB bowl (¥1,600) comes with very tender chicken breast, and there's a Mexican bowl (¥1,480). An acai bowl (¥1,600) comes half-frozen with banana, berries, kiwi, coconut and granola; honey is only added if you say yes. Order and pay at the register, then sit anywhere.

places.notes: [Thai · Namba's long-running Thai house by Nankai station] A 43-seat Thai restaurant thirty seconds from Nankai Namba's south exit, open since 2001. The shop says it is certified by Thailand's Ministry of Commerce, with Thai chefs cooking over 100 dishes. A repeat visitor calls the tom yum kung (¥1,680) the standout, with sourness and heat in balance. The khao man gai (¥1,280) comes with a house sauce in a northeastern style instead of sweet chili. There's also crab-rich poo pad pong curry, a spicy glass-noodle salad, stir-fried water spinach (¥1,380), pad see ew and laksa. The pad thai lunch (¥1,100) includes spring rolls, chicken, salad and soup. The shop says it can cook vegetarian and halal dishes, so ask ahead. Cilantro comes only on request. The menu is in Japanese with photos.

chef_bio.background: Shop text: certified by the Ministry of Commerce of the Thai government; experienced Thai chefs; over 100 dishes.

places.cuisine: Kishu-duck ramen from Gion, Kyoto · light (clear, amber shio) or rich duck broth · house-made German-rye noodles · duck loin and thigh chashu, choose your slices · duck tsukemen with Kishu mikan or cherry sauce · Namba-only duck skewers with grape pepper, yuzu and black shichimi · GION DUCK BEER · Kyoto hojicha with refills
places.notes: [Ramen · Kyoto's Kishu-duck ramen in Sennichimae] The Namba branch of Gion Duck Noodles, a duck-ramen shop from Gion in Kyoto, where bowls arrive dressed like a French plate with pink duck, sprouts and edible flowers. Choose a light broth (a clear, amber shio of pure Kishu duck) or a thick, rich one. Both come on house-made noodles blended with German rye, nutty and almost soba-like, with grape pepper on the rim to stir in. The duck chashu comes as loin and thigh, and you pick how many slices of each. The tsukemen takes a different direction: rye flat noodles in a creamy duck dip with a Kishu-mikan or cherry sauce and a Madeira accent. The Namba-only duck skewers come with three condiments, and there's a house GION DUCK BEER. The menu uses emoji, and staff explain it. Cashless.

chef_bio.background: Gion Duck Noodles; Namba branch with exclusive duck skewers (August–September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a clear soup with a strong duck flavor, featuring a refined richness that feels more like French cuisine than traditional ramen. The noodles are homemade, made with a blend of German rye." — August 2026.
"What stood out the most was the combination with a sauce made from Kishu mikan… the sauce made with Madeira wine adds an accent." — October 2026, duck tsukemen.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura across from Takashimaya, open late] A 37-seat Kamukura opposite Namba Takashimaya, open from 10 am until 11:30 pm, or 1 am on Fridays and Saturdays, with a queue even near 11 pm. It's the chain's light soy broth, sweet with napa cabbage, and the usual order is the "delicious ramen" or the chashu ramen, a light end to a night of drinking. There's also a half fried rice and gyoza set with garlicky gyoza. Seasonal bowls rotate: a summer cold ramen whose cabbage turns crunchy, almost pickle-like (opinions split), and an autumn hot-and-sour noodle soup. Service is fast, though it's popular with tourists and can get noisy. QR payment only, no cards.

places.notes: [Ramen · Kyoto-duck bowls named after music, west Shinsaibashi] A six-seat basement counter in Nishi-Shinsaibashi that names its bowls after music genres, with a line before opening. "Hip Hop" is a light Kyoto-duck and chicken-bone soy ramen, more refreshing than the name suggests, with duck and pork chashu and a good seasoned egg. "Punk" (¥1,250, October 2026) blends clam and Kyoto-duck broth, finished with a pat of butter on the clams; one repeat visitor says the clam is the star. Both come on smooth, chewy medium-thick flat noodles. A summer "Cold R&B" (¥1,200) served everything ice-cold with rare chashu and long menma. Buy a ticket; cash only. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

places.notes: [Ramen · late-night chicken-paitan food truck in back-street Namba] A ramen food truck parked behind a lot under the elevated expressway, two minutes from Osaka Namba, with tables and chairs out front like an old yatai. Open since April 2026, it runs until 2 am and already draws repeat customers. The chicken paitan is thick and smooth, rich without a heavy aftertaste, on wavy medium-thick noodles. It comes as shoyu, garlic shoyu or a shellfish-based version, mostly ¥1,200. A sweet-seasoned rare chashu makes you want rice; there's a seared chashu bowl (¥1,200), set A (¥1,350) and an oddly addictive mazesoba. Kimchi, chopped onion, vinegar and sesame on the table change the bowl as you go. It's hidden when cars are parked in front. Cash only.

anecdotes.text: "You can really taste the deliciousness of the chicken, with a smooth and rich flavor in the thick broth. Despite being rich, it has no unpleasant aftertaste." — September 2026, rich soy toripaitan.

"Located under the elevated tracks in Namba, behind a parking lot, this place can be a bit hidden when cars are parked! Despite that, regular customers keep coming in!" — October 2026, shellfish-based toripaitan ¥1,200.

places.notes: [Ramen · all-night garlic tonkotsu at the east end of Dotonbori] A small ramen shop at the Nippombashi end of Dotonbori, open until 4 am and around the clock on Fridays and Saturdays. Reviewers who miss the old Satsuma-kko on Dotonbori come here. The bowl is a soy-tonkotsu on medium-thin straight noodles, called light by one reviewer and rich-but-smooth by another. The thick, moist chashu is why regulars come; one says they come for the chashu more than the ramen. Ramen is ¥1,100, large ¥1,380, and kimchi ¥400 (September–October 2026); some find it pricey for what it is. Cash only.

The abura-soba (¥850, June 2026) arrives within minutes of handing over your ticket. It's chewy noodles in a light sauce that you build up with plenty of vinegar and chili oil, plus spicy miso and garlic from the table. One fan swears by the egg topping, and kimchi works too. Reviewers call it cheap next to ramen and easy for abura-soba first-timers. It gets crowded in the afternoon, with tourists too, and the wait can be long. Cash only.

places.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's 24-hour dragon-sign classic] One of the long-running Kinryu Ramen shops of Namba, under the giant dragon sign and open around the clock. The menu is just Kinryu ramen (¥900, October 2026) or chashu ramen. Buy a ticket by the door, hand it in, and collect your bowl when called. The broth is a white pork-and-chicken soup with soy, lighter than it looks and smooth rather than greasy, with two kinds of chashu even in the regular bowl. The fun is at the counter: free, unlimited kimchi, spicy garlic chives, garlic and rice, which turn the mild soup into a stamina bowl. You sit on low tatami platforms without backrests, and you might wonder about shoes. It's built for after drinking, or a ten-minute breakfast.

The ramen and fried rice set is ¥1,220, and an after-work quick-drink set (beer plus a chashu, menma, egg and kimchi platter, then ramen) is ¥1,380. Another found the taste and service simply average.

places.notes: [Ramen · vegan, gluten-free ramen in Bakuromachi] A spacious, clean ramen shop that opened on 29 January 2026, a new concept from MERCY Vegan Factory. Everything is plant-based and free of the five pungent vegetables, and the ramen is gluten-free. The noodles are medium-thick curly rice-flour noodles from Hokkaido, chewy and bouncy. The shio ramen (¥1,870) is a light, low-viscosity kombu broth with a touch of lemon. The yakuzen soy-milk dan dan noodles (¥2,420; ¥2,200 in July) come loaded with vegetables and warming herbs but only mildly spicy. Summer 2026 added a sesame-vinegar cold noodle (¥2,200). Prices are high for ramen, and one visitor switched to lemonade and salt bread. Outside the ramen, a sister shop's release warns that some items may contain wheat, so ask.

places.notes: [Vegan · all-vegan organic set meals near Yotsubashi] A long-running all-vegan organic restaurant, open since 2014, two minutes from Yotsubashi Station. It's natural and stylish inside, with a shaded terrace deck and a retail shelf by the door. The most popular order is the soy-meat kara-age set: fried in premium canola oil with a house Japanese-style sauce, organic soy-milk mayonnaise and organic sesame. It comes with an organic salad, low-sodium miso soup and pesticide-free brown rice. The soy-meat hamburg with vegan cheese is hearty enough to win over meat-eaters. The menu is wide, and a vegetarian visitor from Australia came back after ten years. Order by QR code at the table. It's popular, so book, especially for lunch. Gluten isn't addressed anywhere, so ask.

chef_bio.philosophy: Organic & vegan food "with care and attention to safety and flavor" (shop text).
